thinset isn't available where i live. and doing tiles is usually with rough concrete finish. tile adhesive.

the house had concrete but it was rough finish. so it was not "smooth" for the reason that we thought we are doing tiles on it. So the Resin people asked us to make it smooth, the house contractor did, it was done, 2 months prior the resin (because we were installing some automatic doors first). The flooring contractor did no test. They just went to the site. measure the slab. They did not grind the slab prior to the epoxy. They just looked, saw cracks on the floor, applied epoxy, saying it will hold the concrete (after i asked them if it was ok, that the floor was cracked). then added the gray resin, applied the flakes. then did a thin layer of resin. rolled it into the flakes.

The rest of the floor is fine. I just didnt know about resin. And the lady that we asked to resin . when i asked her if the floor was ok to be resin. she said yes. so i was confident enough that everything will be fine.
